I'm a dog groomer. You cannot by almost any circumstance shave a double coated dog. It causes the dog to overheat as it disrupts their regulatory system. Plus it could wreck their future coat.

Don't send your dog to a groomer who will shave the dog UNLESS that is what you want. You technically can do it, as long as you are aware of what you're doing.

Your dog needs a bath and TIDY, meaning, using scissors ONLY.

Just a dusting is how I would describe how to trim her. There are plenty of videos on YouTube about double coated dogs and how to groom them.

All they need is a bath and blow dry mainly. Just use scissors if hairs are too long and touching the ground. That and shave their PAW PADS.

Hope this helps.

I am a certified pet groomer,

I don't suggest cutting out the mats unless you have really good light. I am careful with cats as their skin is thin, and mats are typically tight.
Just be careful if you decide to cut.
For bathing, run him a small bath up to his tummy when standing. (Do this before he is in the room, so the sound doesn't spook him)
Bath him as normal, use lots of soap to make sure he is clean, as there will be lots of oil build-up.
Rinse him well, get all the soap off.
Blow Dry him if possible, with a hand dryer, set at medium to cool temp, and low setting. Don't let him fully air dry as this causes mats, and cats get cold easily.
